item.title: Multi-Threading with Web Workers
item.description: We’ve repeated it several times throughout these notes: JavaScript is single-threaded. Normally, that’s fine. But what happens if you need to process a 50MB CSV file, apply image blur filters, or run heavy cryptographic hashing in the browser? If you run that loop on the main thread, the entire browser tab completely freezes. Buttons stop clicking, typing halts, and the dreaded “Page Unresponsive” popup appears. :') The solution? Offload heavy calculations onto genuine background threads using Web Workers.

item.title: Modern Lazy Loading with Intersection Observer
item.description: Remember how we used to build lazy loading before 2019? We would attach an event listener to window.addEventListener('scroll', ...), repeatedly call element.getBoundingClientRect(), and calculate offsets manually. Every single scroll event caused browser layout thrashing. It worked, but it felt clunky and consumed unnecessary battery on mobile devices. :') Enter the Intersection Observer API. What Does It Do? Instead of continuously polling scroll coordinates on the main thread, the browser itself asynchronously monitors when a target element enters or exits the visible screen viewport!

item.title: Event Optimization: Debounce vs Throttle
item.description: Ever hooked an event listener to a search input or a window scroll, and watched your browser tab turn into an airplane jet engine? :v Events like input, scroll, and mousemove fire dozens of times per second. If every single keystroke triggers an expensive API request or complex DOM recalculation, your interface will lag and your server will hate you. The remedy? Debounce and Throttle. Let’s break down the difference with practical code you can drop into any project.

item.title: Event Delegation & Bubbling
item.description: Here’s a puzzle for you: what happens if you have a list of 500 items and each needs a delete button? Do you run a loop and attach 500 individual addEventListener calls to each button? Well… you could, but your browser’s memory won’t be too thrilled with you. :v There’s a smarter, much more elegant trick: Event Delegation. How Events Travel: Bubbling Up When you click an element nested deep inside the DOM, the event doesn’t just stop there.

item.title: Standard Library - Worker Threads
item.description: Halo semua, kembali lagi bersama Author :') Inilah catatan penutup untuk rangkaian seri pembelajaran NodeJS Standard Library kita! Salah satu kritik terbesar orang terhadap NodeJS di masa lalu adalah: “NodeJS itu single-threaded, ngga cocok buat komputasi berat (CPU-intensive task)!" Kalau ada perhitungan matematika jutaan iterasi, seluruh server bakal macet dan request user lain ngga bisa masuk. Tapi sejak kehadiran modul worker_threads, anggapan itu resmi dipatahkan! NodeJS sekarang memiliki dukungan resmi untuk komputasi paralel sejati memanfaatkan seluruh core prosesor di CPU kita.

item.title: Standard Library - Stream
item.description: Halo semua, kembali lagi bersama Author :') Pernah ngga kalian membayangkan bagaimana cara server memproses file video atau file data raksasa berukuran 5 GB? Kalau kita membaca seluruh file 5 GB itu sekaligus memakai fs.readFile(), maka RAM server kita bakal langsung tersedot habis 5 GB saat itu juga! Kalau ada 4 orang saja yang mengunduh bersamaan, server langsung mogok karena Out of Memory. :v Solusi elegan untuk masalah ini adalah: Stream.
